title: Quiet G before N
kidRule: When G comes right before N at the start or the end of a word, the G usually stays quiet and N does all the talking! (In the middle of a word, like SIGNAL, you can hear it.)
hint: We hear '/n/', but a quiet letter is hiding right before the N. Which one?
reminder: A quiet G hides right before the N, so we write G-N.

check.question: Why can't we hear the G in DESIGN?
check.correctAnswer: G usually stays quiet when it comes right before N at the start or end of a word!
distractors: Because G is always quiet in long words
Because the letter I makes the G quiet

words.def: To chew on something again and again.
words.sent: Beavers gnaw on trees with their strong teeth.
words.story: A beaver's front teeth never stop growing, so chewing on wood keeps them from getting too long!
words.card: '*Aw*, please do not *gnaw* my pencil!' I begged the hamster.

words.def: To plan how something will look or work before you make it.
words.sent: We will design a rocket out of cardboard boxes.
words.story: Before people ride a new roller coaster, the builders send it around the track carrying dummies filled with water!
words.card: I will *design* a giant *sign* that says 'Beware of the ticklish dragon!'

words.def: To put things in a straight line.
words.sent: Please align your shoes neatly by the door.
words.story: Sometimes several planets seem to line up in the night sky, and people call it a planet parade!
words.card: My pal *Al* likes to *align* his peas before he eats them!

words.def: To say that you are giving up a job or a game.
words.sent: The coach chose to resign after ten years with the team.
words.story: In chess, a player can resign from a losing game by gently tipping over their own king!
words.card: The tired stop *sign* wanted to *resign* and become a go *sign*!

words.def: The time when a king or queen rules a country.
words.sent: During her reign the queen built many schools.
words.story: Queen Elizabeth the Second ruled for 70 years, longer than any other British king or queen!
words.card: The frog king's *reign* was so soggy that he had to *re*paint his throne every day!
words.trick: A kinG has a reiGN: remember the G before the N!

words.sent: My aunt collects foreign coins from her trips.
words.story: About 7,000 different languages are spoken around the world today!
words.card: I traded my sandwich *for* a *foreign* coin with a kangaroo on it!

words.def: A big African animal with curved horns, a beard, and a long tail. It is also called a wildebeest.
words.sent: The gnu ran across the grassy plain with its herd.
words.story: Every year more than a million of these animals walk across Africa together, looking for fresh grass!
words.card: The *gnu* wore a tutu and juggled pea*nu*ts at the zoo!

words.def: To grind your teeth together, often when you are angry.
words.sent: The grumpy troll began to gnash his teeth.
words.story: Some people grind their teeth together while they are fast asleep and never even know it!
words.card: Dragons *gnash* their teeth when their toast turns to *ash*!

words.def: To give someone a job to do.
words.sent: Our teacher will assign each of us a classroom job.
words.story: Astronauts on the space station are given chores too. They even have to vacuum!
words.card: The king will *assign* a dragon to paint the castle *sign* pink!

words.def: Twisted, bumpy, and rough, like an old tree root.
words.sent: The old tree had gnarly roots that stuck out of the ground.
words.story: Surfers started using this word for a big, scary wave, and now some people say it to mean 'awesome'!
words.card: The *nar*whal bumped his horn on a *gnarly* old shipwreck!
